name: Starter: Swedish
about: Swedish word order in real, everyday sentences.

words.åka: to go (by car, bus or train)
words.stå: to stand, to be (of upright things)
words.laga: to cook, to prepare (food); to repair

hur-mår-du.about: A greeting you learn whole: literally, how feel you? Answer with Bra, tack (fine, thanks).

vad-heter-du.about: Literally, what are you called? Answer with Jag heter and your name.

ursäkta.about: To get someone's attention, or to get past them.

i-morgon.about: Also written imorgon. morgon alone is morning.

i-helgen.about: helg is weekend; i helgen is this one (or the last one, said about the past).

det-finns.about: For what exists or can be found somewhere: Det finns kaffe i köket.

smaklig-måltid.about: Said before eating; literally, tasty meal.

thanks-thank-you-please-after-a-request.en: thanks, thank you; please (after a request)

items.means: A coffee, thank you very much.

concept.line: The present is the same for every person and usually ends in -r (jag bor, hon bor); it means both I live and I'm living.
In a yes/no question the verb that shows the tense comes first; after a question word it comes before the subject (unless the question word is the subject).
min, din and vår match the noun: min pappa (an en word), vårt hus (an ett word), mina nycklar (plural).
The word for the is an ending on the noun: bil, bilen (the car); hus, huset (the house).
After vill, kan, måste, ska and får, the next verb is a plain infinitive, with no att.
Adjectives match what they describe: en stor bil, ett stort kök, stora hus, den stora bilen; det counts as an ett word, so det är kallt.
